text:
morgan: Heads-up — onboarding report: fresh Mac M1 user installs the sample app from our internal index and import fails immediately with dlopen error. Repro on CI macos-arm matrix.

Error snippet:
```
ImportError: dlopen(/Users/runner/work/_temp/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/_kv_native.cpython-311-darwin.so, 0x0002): symbol not found: _kv_native_init
  Referenced from: /Users/.../_kv_native.cpython-311-darwin.so
  Expected in: flat namespace
```

lee: did they pip install from https://pkgstore.redwood.internal/simple? Our index sometimes builds wheel artifacts from sdists and the builder marks them as py3-none-any if it misses native extensions. That would make pip pick a wheel that looks pure but contains a platform .so.

jamie: yep, our release job currently uploads the sdist and lets pkgstore build wheels. If the builder ran on x86 runners it will produce x86 mac wheels but tag could still be universal/any. Ugly.

devops-bot: CI job nightly/samples/macos-arm #789 failed — import error on sample-app import (automated).

morgan: Temporary workaround for users: `pip install --no-binary :all: redwood-sdk` or `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` to force a local build. Not great for quickstarts.

lee: long term we should: 1) build platform-specific wheels during release (cibuildwheel), 2) upload explicit wheel files to pkgstore, 3) add a publish-time validation that rejects any `py3-none-any.whl` that contains compiled extensions.

jamie: also check pyproject/build backend configuration. If setuptools_scm / poetry generate sdist-only artifacts, the index builder needs correct setup.cfg / bdist_wheel options (root_is_pure=false) so tags are correct.

morgan: I'll add a tiny import smoke test in the sample-app CI matrix for macos-arm so this surfaces earlier. Also writing a KB note for support: "If you get dlopen symbol errors on Apple Silicon, reinstall from source or use --no-binary until release pipeline patch."

jamie: assigning the pipeline tickets to myself — will add cibuildwheel and an artifact sanity-check job. Putting a quick PR for the publish hook that scans wheels for `.so` and fails if tag is `py3-none-any`.

lee: thanks. this should cut down onboarding pain. :raised_hands:
